repairs.before: His elder half-brother Murong Han, who held the title general who establishes might, was a brilliant warrior whom Huang resented, while his full brothers Murong Ren and Murong Zhao, both favored by Hui, also stirred his jealousy.
repairs.after: Earlier, Huang's elder half-brother Murong Han, general who establishes might, was brave in arms and of heroic talent, and Huang had long resented him. Huang's younger full brothers Murong Ren, general who campaigns against the caitiffs, and Murong Zhao, general who extends martial power, were both favored by Hui, which also displeased Huang.
repairs.sourceQuote: 初，皝庶兄建威翰驍武有雄才，素為皝所忌，母弟征虜仁、廣武昭並有寵於廆，皝亦不平之。
repairs.reason: The proposal correctly restores 初 (Earlier), 素 (long), the offices 建威/征虜/廣武, and 母弟 as younger brothers by the same mother as Huang. Two fixes: 驍武有雄才 has two propositions (brave in arms; heroic talent), and 'brilliant warrior' drops the second. 'His younger full brothers' is ambiguous after a sentence about Han, who is a concubine's son, so it now reads 'Huang's'. 亦不平之 = Huang was also displeased with them. Names stay separate from offices; actors unchanged.
repairs.pairedFieldChecked: In the beginning, Huang’s elder half-brother by a concubine, Jianwei Han, was fierce in arms and had heroic talent; he had long been envied by Huang; younger brothers by the same mother, Ren the Campaign General and Zhao the Guangwu general, both had favor with Hui; Huang also was not even toward them.

repairs.after: At first, Huang's elder brother by a concubine, Han, the general who establishes might, was brave in warfare and had heroic talent; Huang had long been jealous of him. His younger brothers by the same mother, Ren, the general who campaigns against the caitiffs, and Zhao, the general who extends martial power, both enjoyed Hui's favor; Huang was also displeased with them.
repairs.sourceQuote: 初，皝庶兄建威翰驍武有雄才，素為皝所忌，母弟征虜仁、廣武昭並有寵於廆，皝亦不平之。
repairs.reason: Every proposition is kept: 初 (At first), 庶兄 (elder brother by a concubine), 建威 as an office separate from the name Han, 驍武 and 有雄才, 素為皝所忌 (long jealous), 母弟 (younger brothers by the same mother, where 'His' follows Huang's as the antecedent in the literal's clause order), 征虜 and 廣武 as offices, 並有寵於廆, and 亦不平之. This also fixes the old 'Campaign General' for 征虜.

repairs.before: Huang dispatched his brother Murong You and Marshal Tong Shou against him.
repairs.after: Huang dispatched his younger brother Murong You, general who establishes martial power, Marshal Tong Shou, and others to campaign against Ren.
repairs.sourceQuote: 皝遣其弟建武幼、司馬佟壽等討之。
repairs.reason: Restores 弟 (younger brother), 建武 as You's abbreviated office (not the reign era of s0007, since it stands before the name in a list of officers), 司馬 Tong Shou, 等 (and others), and 討 (campaign against). 之 = Ren, who fled to Pingguo in s0015 and fights You in s0017. 'Establishes martial power' (建武) stays distinct from 'establishes might' (建威) and 'extends martial power' (廣武).
repairs.pairedFieldChecked: Huang sent his younger brother Jianwu You, marshal Tong Shou, and others to campaign against him.

repairs.sourceQuote: 皝遣其弟建武幼、司馬佟壽等討之。
repairs.reason: Separates the office 建武 from the personal name 幼 and keeps 弟, 司馬, 等 and 討之 exactly. Leaving 之 as 'him' is acceptable for the literal field; the referent (Ren) is clear from s0015.
